newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: First black stockbroking firm starts in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: First black stockbroking firm starts in S.Africa.

text.p: South Africa's first black stockbroking firm was officially launched on Thursday in a further step towards economic empowerment of the black majority.
Legae securities (Pty) Ltd is scheduled to start business on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) around September 17.
"This is a history-making deal. It's been tough, but we have succeeded," managing director Emmanuel Lediga told Reuters.
As the first black floor trader on the JSE, Lediga already knows a fair bit about breaking into the former bastions of white power
"We have formed a firm that black people can call their own...we are committed to bringing blacks and women in to our ranks," he said.
Lediga and co-founder finance director Ramasimong Tau hold a controlling stake of 60.5 percent of Legae's shares with minority interests held by HSBC James Capel and chairman Randle Carter.
The firm is capitalised at about three million rand ($665,000).

"The partners are prepared to inject more capital as the firm expands. The directors expect Legae Securities to experience fast growth in the first few years of its operations," the firm said in a statement.
The official launch of Legae comes hot on the heels of a landmark deal for black empowerment in South Africa.

Last week the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC), representing 50 black economic interest groups, won control of the giant industrial holding group Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd in a three billion rand deal.

Lediga said Legae would seek to combine a normal portfolio of stockbroking activities together with an emphasis on emerging black businesses. "We have set up a broking firm that can be unique in serving both these markets," he said.
Equities industry industry sources said share ownership remains almost exclusively a white reserve.
But Legae predicted more black stockbroking firms would follow in his. "It is going to be hard, but I am sure others will follow," he said.
